correctness.rationale: A unit coefficient f is restricted nilpotent just when the coefficient of t^(p−1) in 1/f is zero: integrating the other terms gives the normal form (1+b u^(p−1))∂u, whose p-power is −b times itself. The condition solves linearly for the last coefficient with invertible coefficient on the unit open, giving G_m × A^(p−2). Valuation one is excluded by the action on (t)/(t²); valuations at least two raise degree. In a bracket with f of valuation r, the initial term for a coefficient of valuation s≠r is f_r g_s(s−r)t^(r+s−1) if that exponent is below p. If s=r, subtract a multiple of f first. This gives the exact centralizer and regular projection using division by the nonzero leading coefficient. For an independent class computation let a=(p−1)/2 and L=[A¹]. Partition triples by the minimum valuation and the first position attaining it. The unit case contributes L^(p−2)(L³−1), and the all-high case (valuation at least a+1) contributes L^(3a), since that ideal is abelian. For each minimum r from 2 through a, the valuation-r entry has base class (L−1)L^(p−r−1); preceding entries range over the high ideal of dimension r−1, and following entries over the abelian centralizer of dimension r. Summing over positions yields (L−1)(1+L+L²)L^(p+r−3). All charts and inverses are regular over k, without perfection assumptions; summing produces the stated class. Point counting over extensions and the exponential definition of the zeta function give the claimed consequences. The uploaded checker is finite diagnostic evidence only and was not executed.
